sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Khwarazmshahs, the line of Anushtigin
sources.note: Indexed original scholarly article: hereditary line1097 to 1231, Seljuk vassalage to1157 and imperial expansion. Public imported-map warning derives from local geometry audit.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Tekesh ibn Il-Arslan
sources.note: Reign1172 to 1200,1194 defeat of ToghrilIII, western resistance after Tekesh death. Not confused with earlier Khwarazmian dynasties.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Terken Khatun
sources.note: Direct article. Wife of Tekesh and mother of MuhammadII, distinct from Tekesh’s own mother of the same title. Military marriage alliance and authority after1200.

sources.title: Turkmenistan State News Agency: Guiding star of Dehistan
sources.note: 22June2013 official archaeological heritage report. Use only reported workshops, water supply, sewage, baths, brick paving and caravanserais. Broad medieval context; exact layers not supplied. Do not use its confused ancient chronology,20ha area or1223 destruction date.

sources.title: UNESCO Tentative Lists: Dehistan / Mishrian
sources.note: Turkmenistan Ministry of Culture submission1998. Tenth to fourteenth-century city; mosque of MuhammadII, earlier minaret1004/5, abandonment15thcentury. Tentative-list submission, not an inscribed World Heritage property.

sources.title: ICOMOS: Kunya-Urgench evaluation, April 2005
sources.note: PDF pp73 to 74 description/history, pp75 to 76 comparisons/conservation. Tekesh attributed mausoleum1195?; conical roof, turquoise and stalactites. Mongol1221 destruction followed by rebuilding. Other monuments later; do not assign entire archaeological park to dynasty.

sources.title: US National Library of Medicine: Jorjani’s medical encyclopedia, MS P5
sources.note: Direct catalogue: Persian title ذخيره خوارزمشاهى and English translation; work composed after1110 for Qutb al-Din Muhammad; ten books. MS P5 title fol1b line11/348b line22,17thcentury witness. Exact AH/CE colophon equivalence appears inconsistent, so no exact copying year used. Typeset catalogue transcription, not claimed autograph or fresh palaeographic reading.

sources.title: Sadeq Sajjadi: Dentistry in Persia
sources.note: Dental medicine before Mongol invasion, Jorjani paragraph: tooth anatomy, milk teeth, teething, oral hygiene/toothpicks; cites Dakhira18 to 19,112,209,387,390. Historical medical interests, no endorsement of remedies.

sources.title: Ali Akbar Saidi Sirjani: Dakhira-ye Khwarazmshahi
sources.note: Paragraphs after ninth book: author’s apology, physician and court pharmacy director, lack of time for travel/plant collection/expert consultation.

sources.title: John R. Perry and colleagues: Dictionaries, Arabic-Persian universal works
sources.note: Universal dictionaries section: Zamakhshari’s Muqaddimat al-adab for Atsiz, categories of nouns/verbs/particles/inflections, synonyms and antonyms, Chorasmian-gloss manuscript. Indexed original full relevant paragraph checked.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Jalal al-Din Khwarazmshah
sources.note: Mongol invasion,1221 Parvan/Indus and flight to India; later western campaigns; August1231 death near Mayyafariqin. Never regained Khwarazm, surviving military contingents not continued royal state.

proposedOverrides.summary: The Anushteginid Khwarazmshahs expanded from Khwarazm into a major empire before Mongol conquest and the last ruler’s death in 1231.

batchIdentityNotes.finding: Exact world1200 import1200 to 1279,63.6000 to 71.4049E/23.6757 to 32.5318N. Southern Afghanistan/Pakistan footprint omits Khwarazm and most historical empire. Public overview explicitly distinguishes map from1097 to 1231 Anushteginid narrative. Existing interval retained only as map_coverage; no repair invented. Earlier Khwarazm dynasties and post1231 military contingents not conflated.
